Subject: Disconnected image sanction and release playbook

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, we're kicking off a short playbook to formalize how EdgeGrid wants to accept and activate disconnected (air-gapped) image bundles from Redwood. The scope for this thread: signed manifest format, who signs, operator acceptance checklist, and the physical handoff window.

Quick asks to unblock timelines:
- Confirm the signing authority on your side (name + role + PGP/SSH key id or HSM slot).
- Do you require customer-side HSM signing, or is a Redwood-provided signature (detached) acceptable for initial rollout?
- Preferred transport: sealed USB + courier, or certified courier with tamper seals? Any carrier preferences.
- Acceptance window at your site (dates/times in PST) and a primary onsite contact.

I've attached an initial manifest template and the SOW draft so you can see fields we'll include in the signed envelope. Once we lock the signing flow, Rishi will prepare a signed test bundle for your ingress team to validate.

Attachments: release_manifest_v1.txt (text/plain), initial_sow_edgegrid_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Proposed next step: show-of-availability call next Tue (23rd) 10:00–11:00 PST to sync on signer roster and transport. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Signing authority: we prefer customer HSM signing for production bundles. Our security ops lead (Tom Reynolds) will be the authority and will sign using our HSM. For initial validation we can accept a Redwood detached signature if you supply an auditable signature chain.

2) Manifest expectations: can you confirm the manifest includes the following fields — bundle_hash (sha256), build_id, build_time (UTC), signer_identity, signer_certificate_fingerprint, and list of component artifacts with individual checksums? We also need the signature envelope to state the algorithm and a versioned schema.

3) Transport: certified courier with tamper-evident seals is preferred. USB is OK but only as a contingency; we need a documented chain-of-custody form.

4) Acceptance window: we can do Nov 24–25 between 08:00–16:00 PST. Tom will be onsite; cc'ed.

We'll review the manifest and SOW and circle back with any redlines by EOD Thu. Please confirm whether Redwood can provide an example signed manifest using ED25519 or RSA-PSS so Tom's team can validate signature parsing libraries.

Best,
Alyssa

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks — quick technical response to address the manifest and signature questions so we can move to a signed test bundle: 

- Manifest schema: yes, we'll include bundle_hash (sha256), build_id, build_time (RFC3339 UTC), signer_identity (CN/email), signer_certificate_fingerprint (sha256), artifact list with per-file sha256 checksums, release_notes reference, and schema_version. We'll attach schema docs to the Drive link (see thread metadata).

- Signature: our recommendation is ED25519 for compactness and wide library support. We can produce both an ED25519 detached signature (RFC 8032 format) and an RSA-PSS signature if you require it for HSM interoperability. The signature envelope will explicitly state algorithm, key id, and a timestamp. Example: {algorithm: "ED25519", key_id: "redwood-prod-2026-11", signature_type: "detached", created_at: "2026-11-19T08:00:00Z"}.

- Who signs: For production, EdgeGrid HSM signing is preferred (Tom Reynolds will sign). For the POC/test bundle we will produce a Redwood-signed detached manifest that your team can validate against the schema. When you confirm Tom's key id / slot, we will prepare a test manifest for both verification flows.

- Transport & acceptance: certified courier with chain-of-custody form is our default. We'll provide an operator checklist for onsite acceptance and a sealed-bag id that maps to the manifest. Proposed acceptance checklist highlights: verify tamper seals, validate manifest hash, verify signature against expected key id, validate artifact checksums, perform smoke-start in isolated network, capture audit logs, and sign operator receipt.

Attachments added for your ingress: signed_bundle_manifest.txt (sample detached signature + manifest), operator_checklist.xlsx (acceptance checklist stub).

We can support key wrapping for HSM transfer (for example, wrap symmetric keys under your HSM public key) or remote signing via an HSM API if you prefer us to trigger signing inside your KMS. Let me know which you'd like and we'll scope the integration.

I'll be available on the 23rd for the sync; if you want a pre-call to walk the team through the sample manifest, we can do that on Monday 22nd at 11:00 PST.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: signed_bundle_manifest.txt (text/plain), operator_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
